I think that two things will prove to be true at once.

1) Anthropic and OpenAI will prove to have very weak business economics under the surface. Come 2027/28, the ROI will simply not be there in large-enough fashion. There will be tons of demand for AI, but endless competition from lack of a substantial-enough barrier to entry will mean a race to the bottom in prices, even if they have great models/products. Google, Meta, everything in the realm of open source, Chinese models, and anyone else under the sun who brings a model forward will compete for use. OpenAI and Anthropic won't be able to prop up the amount of spend inherent in their businesses because of falling prices from competition.

2) Even with bad economics, OpenAI and Anthropic's products will remain very important to the USA and others. Being among the most advanced models means that there are certain things that their models will be best for. At least some advanced use-cases will likely show preference towards these models, and may even label them as necessary.

My tinfoil hat tells me that these businesses will IPO and, soon after, their profitability will show cracks. We will see a lot of red in the markets that will serve as an opportunity for buying because ultimately it will not disrupt the momentum of AI in general. Many stocks will crash, including the hyperscalers, and a year later we will be talking about how much of an overreaction it was. Kind of like the tarrif selloff of April 2025.

When OpenAI and Anthropic's stocks eventually fall, other large companies who can benefit by incorporating/utilizing their models, and who can support their continued development with their other cash flow generative business segments, will acquire them. $AAPL, $AMZN , and $MSFT come to mind as possibilities. Once all of that is done and behind us, the market will need to find another wall of worry to climb. And climb it will.
